_about: The Breakdown (studied from 'Phantasic AI training #2', see engine/templates/breakdown.md): a fast numbered teaching reel. One word on screen at a time (sans, ~1 in 4 in serif italic) under the face, a navy title card on the hook, full-screen chapter cards with a giant low-contrast serif numeral that switch colour per step (navy -> paper -> electric blue), a typewriter label over the promise, the CTA keyword pinned in a red-purple-blue gradient to the end, punch-ins every ~1.2 s, SFX only on section changes, an ~88 BPM bed at -13 dB. Footage keeps its own colour.

director.plan: core/scripts/breakdown_plan.py <project> writes every beat: title card, label, chapter cards, CTA pin, serif words.
director.chapters: {type:scene, kind:chapter, num, tone: navy|paper|blue|cream, serif:[words]} from the spoken 'number one/two/three', 'first/second/third', 'step one...' to the end of that clause (1.2-2.4 s).
director.rules: Everything on screen is spoken. SFX only on the title, chapters and the CTA. Footage keeps its own colour.
director.style: The Breakdown: a numbered teaching cut on navy and paper. Cut on sentence starts so each point begins cleanly; no talking-head stretch runs longer than about 3.5 s without the picture changing.
director.restraint: The structure is the numerals; the words are the speaker's. Everything on screen is spoken. No icons, no B-roll, no stickers, no invented names.
director.hook: One `title` scene over the first seconds: the strongest one or two words said in the first 4 s, at most 2 s long.
director.pages: Fill the gaps so no stretch of plain footage runs past ~3.5 s: a `wordpage` for a short punchy clause, a `highlight` page for a longer line the point rests on.
director.cta: A closing ask the speaker actually makes ("comment", "follow", "subscribe", "save this") belongs in the banner, not a scene.
